name: scope

findings.message: claim_coordinator_claim and claim_coordinator_release still use claimed:<machine> labels, not zbuild:claimed — the design for this issue explicitly says to change these functions ('Change claim_coordinator_claim to use the single shared label zbuild:claimed instead of claimed:<machine>'), but only an addition at the bottom of the file was made.
findings.trigger: Any caller that invokes claim_coordinator_claim directly (tests/e2e/claim-race-test.sh calls it in every spawned subshell) still writes claimed:<machine> labels, leaving the plugin's public API inconsistent with the README and ADR-005 that now say the shared label is zbuild:claimed.

findings.message: core/claim/claim.sh was not registered in config/shape-change-paths.txt; the design for this issue states 'Register core/claim/claim.sh in config/shape-change-paths.txt', but the file was not changed.
findings.quote:
config/templates/*.yaml
core/pipeline/template.sh
core/pipeline/runner.sh
core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
core/dispatch/*.sh
config/event-schema.json
findings.trigger: A change to core/claim/claim.sh will not trigger the shape-test suite because the file is absent from shape-change-paths.txt, so a future edit that breaks the pipeline's claim-and-refuse sequence can pass CI without running the shape tests.

knocked_down.message: plugin.sh sources claim.sh at load time via a $(cd ...) subshell, which the design decision for this issue explicitly prohibits: 'plugin.sh must not source core/claim/claim.sh — that would create a circular dependency and add a startup $(cd ...) subshell in plugin.sh's load path.'
knocked_down.quote:
_ccgl_plugin_dir="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../../core/claim/claim.sh
source "$_ccgl_plugin_dir/../../../core/claim/claim.sh"
unset _ccgl_plugin_dir
knocked_down.trigger: Any code that sources plugin.sh directly (the race test does this in every subshell spawned by _race_one) now forks a $(cd ...) subshell at load time and pulls in the entire claim.sh module, creating the plugin→claim→plugin circular load chain the design said to avoid. Under set -euo pipefail the subshell failure path (2>/dev/null || true; pwd) silently leaves _ccgl_plugin_dir empty when cd fails, making the subsequent source fail.
knocked_down.why: The circular load chain cannot occur. When plugin.sh is sourced, `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_GH_LABELS_LOADED=1` is set at line 7, before the bottom-of-file `source claim.sh` executes. When claim.sh then runs, its guard checks the flag and skips sourcing plugin.sh. The finding's described bad outcome (the circular chain) is stopped by this guard. The `_ccgl_plugin_dir` empty-variable scenario is also wrong: `|| true; pwd` ensures `pwd` always runs and produces output whether or not `cd` succeeds.

knocked_down.message: zbuild_claim_release does not unset _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED before calling _ccgl_remove_label; the design says 'unsets _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED before calling _ccgl_remove_label (advisory). Unsetting first makes a second call a no-op', but _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is never unset in the function.
knocked_down.quote:
# Only release if this process acquired the claim
    [[ -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}" ]] && return 0

    # Remove zbuild:claimed (advisory; failures never abort the run)
    _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "zbuild:claimed" || true

    return 0
knocked_down.trigger: If zbuild_claim_release is called twice (e.g. from two different exit paths before the trap '' TERM guard blocks re-entry), _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is still set after the first call so the second call repeats the _ccgl_remove_label invocation rather than being a no-op as the design intended.
knocked_down.why: The double-call trigger cannot occur. `zbuild_claim_release` has only one call site in the entire codebase — inside `_runner_abort_trap`. The very first action of `_runner_abort_trap` is `_runner_restore_stderr`, which sets `trap '' INT TERM`; `zbuild_claim_release` is called hundreds of lines later, well after TERM is already blocked. There is no window where a second TERM could re-enter before the guard is active, and no second code path that calls `zbuild_claim_release`.
